smear.title: The bursts arrive shuffled in time
smear.caption: Every burst is loud enough. The 1,800 Hz bursts arrive 3.24 samples late, more than twice the fax’s 1.5-sample window, and slide into the next burst.

wheel-phase.title: Phase: the output’s dot trails the input’s
wheel-phase.caption: At 1,800 Hz the notch shrinks the wheel to 70.1% (the gain) and sets the dot back 45.5° (the phase): 45.5° ÷ 81° = 0.56 samples late.

phase-lines.title: Phase from the lines
phase-lines.caption: Phase = the pole lines’ directions added up, minus the zero lines’ directions added up: 54.2° − 45.0° = 9.2° at 1,000 Hz.

linear-phase.title: Straight phase lines mean equal delay
linear-phase.caption: A straight phase line through zero is linear phase: every tone delayed the same. The notch is not straight.

burst-tones.title: A burst is many neighboring tones
burst-tones.caption: Switching a tone on and off adds its neighbors. The shorter the burst, the wider its cluster of tones.

catch-up.title: Two tones, one swell, and the notch
catch-up.caption: Before and after the notch: the wiggles move about half a sample, but the swell moves 11.6° ÷ 4.5° = 2.58 samples.

group-delay.title: Group delay is the steepness of the phase
group-delay.caption: The steeper the phase climbs, the later a burst arrives there. That steepness is the group delay.

symmetry.title: Symmetric coefficients balance on the middle
symmetry.caption: Pairs balance on the middle sample: one sample late for every tone.

all-pass.title: An all-pass keeps one ratio everywhere
all-pass.caption: Wherever the tone sits, its zero distance is 1.54 times its pole distance, so the all-pass passes every tone at 100%.

swing.title: Lines swing fastest near the pole
swing.caption: Like your head as a car drives past: the lines whip round when the tone passes near the pole, and barely turn when it is far away.

delay-fix.title: The all-pass fills in where the notch is early
delay-fix.caption: The all-pass holds back the bottom of the band, so the whole line fits the fax’s 1.5-sample window: 4.72 to 5.67 samples.

minimum-phase.title: Same gains, different timing
minimum-phase.caption: Same gains; A’s sound comes first. A, with its zero inside, is minimum phase.

inverse.title: Running the all-pass backwards is unstable
inverse.caption: Swap the all-pass’s poles and zeros and the zero at 1.54 becomes a pole outside the circle: every echo grows.
